samples.stimulus: The table shown describes a study of whether a daily ear-training app improves pitch accuracy scores among musicians. Every participant either was given a daily ear-training app or was not, and every participant was classified as improved or not improved.
samples.question: Which statement best explains what can be concluded about a daily ear-training app from this experiment?
options: Participants who chose a daily ear-training app may differ in other ways (for example, some musicians practice longer), so a difference other than a daily ear-training app could explain the result.
The study cannot support any conclusion because it had fewer than 200 participants.
Because more participants improved with a daily ear-training app, the study proves that a daily ear-training app works for all musicians at a conservatory.
Because participants were randomly assigned, other differences between the conditions should be balanced, so a daily ear-training app likely caused the improvement.
samples.answer: Because participants were randomly assigned, other differences between the conditions should be balanced, so a daily ear-training app likely caused the improvement.
samples.explanation: (1) 개선 비율: 처치 39/50, 비처치 30/60 로 처치 쪽이 높다. (2) 배정 방법: 무작위. (3) 무작위 배정이면 다른 차이가 두 조건에 고르게 나뉜다. (4) 참가자 수나 개선 인원은 인과 판단의 근거가 아니다. (5) 따라서 처치가 원인일 가능성이 높다. 따라서 정답은 D이다.
